gloss: sacred object of worship enshrined in a Shinto shrine

definitions.gloss: sacred object; object of worship; divine body
definitions.explanation: A physical object enshrined in a Shinto shrine that is believed to house or represent a deity (kami). Common examples include mirrors, swords, jewels, stones, and natural objects such as mountains or trees.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{御神体|ごしんたい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{鏡|かがみ}→鏡：02190_kagami⟧だ。
examples.english: The sacred object of this shrine is a mirror.

examples.japanese: {御神体|ごしんたい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一般|いっぱん}→一般：01737_ippan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{参拝者|さんぱいしゃ}→参拝者：21620_sanpaisha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{公開|こうかい}→公開：11665_koukai⟧⟦されていない→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The sacred object is not open to the general public.

examples.japanese: ⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦そのもの→そのもの：27432_sonomono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{御神体|ごしんたい}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧{祀|まつ}る⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{日本各地|にほんかくち}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Shrines that enshrine an entire mountain as a sacred object exist throughout Japan.

notes:
A compound of {御|ご} (honorific prefix), {神|しん} (deity), and ⟦{体|たい}→体：09872_tai⟧ (body). Literally 'the body of the deity.' The {御|ご} prefix reflects the deep reverence with which these objects are treated.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {御神体|ごしんたい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{祀|まつ}る: to enshrine the sacred object
- {御神体|ごしんたい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{拝|おが}む→拝む：00328_ogamu⟧: to worship the sacred object
- {御神体|ごしんたい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{安置|あんち}→安置：18721_anchi⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧: the sacred object is enshrined
- ⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{御神体|ごしんたい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to regard a mountain as the sacred object

TYPES OF 御神体:
- ⟦{鏡|かがみ}→鏡：02190_kagami⟧: mirror (the most common type)
- {剣|つるぎ}: sword
- ⟦{玉|たま}→玉：02221_tama⟧: jewel
- ⟦{石|いし}→石：02177_ishi⟧: stone
- ⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧: mountain (e.g., {三輪山|みわやま} at {大神神社|おおみわじんじゃ})

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {御神体|ごしんたい} is typically kept hidden in the innermost sanctuary (⟦{本殿|ほんでん}→本殿：13090_honden⟧) of a shrine and is rarely, if ever, shown to the public. This secrecy itself is part of Shinto tradition — the unseen nature of the object reinforces its sacred status. The concept reflects the Shinto belief that ⟦{神|かみ}→神：02147_kami⟧ can dwell in physical objects and natural phenomena.
